mainTopic: How many offerings are brought when the court rules wrongly and the people follow it, and which court's ruling creates this obligation
overview: The amud finishes the משנה's argument between רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון about how many פרים and שעירים are brought when בית דין rules wrongly and the people follow. It covers the case of seven tribes and the case of a single tribe's own court. The חכמים say only בית דין הגדול's ruling creates this obligation. The גמרא then brings a ברייתא: if the judges forgot which ruling was wrong, they bring nothing, because the sin itself must become known. The ברייתא gives each תנא's source from the word 'קהל' and explains what counts as a majority. The גמרא asks whether the 'sin must be known' rule fits רבי אליעזר, and רב אשי shows that it can. Finally it explains each opinion by how many times the תנא counts 'קהל': four for רבי יהודה, three for רבי שמעון and two for רבי מאיר. It ends with two פסוקים behind רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule about six or seven tribes.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: thirteen bulls for a mistake of the whole community
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון finishes the first argument of the משנה. One bull is brought for each of the twelve tribes and one for the court, which makes thirteen. For עבודה זרה it is thirteen bulls and thirteen goats.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: thirteen bulls. For idol worship: thirteen bulls and thirteen goats. That is a bull and a goat for every tribe, and a bull and a goat for the court.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives רבי שמעון's opinion in its earlier case, where the community sinned by following the court's mistaken ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון counts each tribe as its own 'community' that brings its own offering. He also says בית דין brings one of its own. So the total is the twelve tribes plus one for the court.

keyTerms.meaning: A bull, the offering brought for a community's mistaken sin
A goat, added when the sin was עבודה זרה
Idol worship
A tribe of Israel

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: שְׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר פָּרִים,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: thirteen bulls,
and for idol worship –

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר פָּרִים וּשְׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר שְׂעִירִים,
phrases.english: thirteen bulls and thirteen goats,
a bull and a goat for each and every tribe,
and a bull and a goat for the court.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: שְׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר פָּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a dispute in the משנה that began before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each tribe brings a bull (and a goat for עבודה זרה), and the court brings one too, for thirteen in total.

steps.title: Seven tribes sin: רבי מאיר says one bull
steps.stepSummary: A new case: seven tribes, or a majority, followed the court's mistaken ruling. רבי מאיר says only one bull is brought, or a bull and a goat for עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the court ruled and seven tribes, or a majority of them, acted on its ruling, they bring one bull. For idol worship they bring a bull and a goat. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens a new case, where only part of the nation sinned. It starts with רבי מאיר's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seven of the twelve tribes count as a majority, so the sin counts as a community sin. For רבי מאיר, one single offering covers the whole nation, just as in the earlier case.

keyTerms.meaning: They issued a ruling
Based on their word, meaning following their ruling
A majority of them

phrases.english: If the court issued a ruling

phrases.aramaic: וְעָשׂוּ שִׁבְעָה שְׁבָטִים אוֹ רוּבָּן עַל פִּיהֶן –
phrases.english: and seven tribes, or a majority of them, acted on its ruling –
they bring a bull,
and for idol worship – they bring a bull and a goat,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹרוּ בֵּית דִּין וְעָשׂוּ שִׁבְעָה שְׁבָטִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the case of the whole community to the case of seven tribes
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When seven tribes sin, one bull is brought (a bull and a goat for עבודה זרה).

steps.title: רבי יהודה: even the tribes that did not sin bring bulls
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says each of the seven sinning tribes brings a bull. Each of the other tribes, which did not sin, also brings a bull because of the sinners.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: the seven tribes that sinned bring seven bulls. The other tribes, which did not sin, also bring a bull because of them. Even those who did not sin bring an offering because of the sinners.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה argues on רבי מאיר in the seven-tribe case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, each tribe counts as its own 'community', so each sinning tribe brings its own bull. He adds something surprising: once a majority sinned, the tribes that did not sin are pulled in too and bring a bull as well.

keyTerms.meaning: That sinned
On their account, because of them
The sinners

steps.confusionAlert: Don't miss this: the tribes that did NOT sin still bring a bull. They bring it because of the sinners, not because of anything they did themselves.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: שִׁבְעָה שְׁבָטִים שֶׁחָטְאוּ – מְבִיאִין שִׁבְעָה פָּרִים,
phrases.english: the seven tribes that sinned – bring seven bulls,
and the rest of the tribes, which did not sin –
bring a bull on their account,
phrases.notes: Each of these other tribes brings its own bull.

phrases.english: for even those who did not sin
bring an offering because of the sinners.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: שִׁבְעָה שְׁבָטִים שֶׁחָטְאוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues on רבי מאיר's opinion in the same case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each sinning tribe brings a bull, and each tribe that did not sin also brings a bull because of the sinners.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: eight bulls for seven tribes
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says only the sinning tribes bring, one bull each, plus one for the court. That makes eight in total, or eight bulls and eight goats for עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: eight bulls. For idol worship: eight bulls and eight goats. That is a bull and a goat for each tribe, and a bull and a goat for the court.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives a third opinion in the seven-tribe case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רבי יהודה, רבי שמעון gives each tribe its own offering. But unlike רבי יהודה, he does not make the tribes that did not sin bring anything. Instead he adds one offering for בית דין, just as he did in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: Eight
Goats

steps.whatToRemember: Seven tribes sinned. רבי מאיר: one bull for everyone. רבי יהודה: one bull for every tribe, even the tribes that did not sin. רבי שמעון: a bull only for each sinning tribe, plus one for the court.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: eight bulls,
and for idol worship –
eight bulls and eight goats,
a bull and a goat for each and every tribe,
phrases.notes: He means each of the seven tribes that sinned.

phrases.english: and a bull and a goat for the court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third opinion in the seven-tribe case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each sinning tribe brings a bull (and a goat), plus one for the court.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: a tribe's own court can make that tribe liable
steps.stepSummary: A new case: the local court of one tribe ruled wrongly and its tribe followed. רבי יהודה says only that tribe is liable, and all the other tribes are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the court of one of the tribes issued a ruling and that tribe acted on it, that tribe is liable and all the other tribes are exempt. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a third case, a mistaken ruling by one tribe's own court, and gives רבי יהודה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי יהודה treats a single tribe as a full 'community'. So the ruling of its own court is enough to obligate that tribe in the community offering. The other tribes had no part in this, so they owe nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Obligated to bring the offering
Exempt

phrases.aramaic: הוֹרוּ בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל אֶחָד מִן הַשְּׁבָטִים,
phrases.english: If the court of one of the tribes issued a ruling,
and that tribe acted on its ruling –
that tribe is liable,
and all the rest of the tribes are exempt,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹרוּ בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל אֶחָד מִן הַשְּׁבָטִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new case: the court of a single tribe
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A tribe that follows its own court's mistaken ruling is liable, and the other tribes are exempt.

steps.title: חכמים: only the בית דין הגדול's ruling creates liability
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים argue. Only a ruling of בית דין הגדול obligates this offering, because the פסוק says 'the whole assembly of Israel'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: there is liability only for rulings of בית דין הגדול alone, as it says: 'And if the whole assembly of Israel errs', and not the assembly of that one tribe.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים argue on רבי יהודה and use a פסוק to prove their view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'the whole assembly of Israel', which points to the court of the whole nation. A tribe's local court is not 'the whole assembly of Israel', so its mistaken ruling does not create liability for this offering.

keyTerms.meaning: The Great Court, the סנהדרין
Rulings
The assembly of Israel
As it is said, introducing a פסוק

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule for the whole מסכת: the special community offering is tied to the national court, the סנהדרין, and not to a local court.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
One is liable only

phrases.aramaic: עַל הוֹרָיוֹת בֵּית דִּין הַגָּדוֹל בִּלְבַד,
phrases.english: for rulings of the Great Court alone,
as it is said: "And if the whole assembly of Israel errs,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:13

phrases.english: and not the assembly of that one tribe.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵין חַיָּיבִין אֶלָּא עַל הוֹרָיוֹת בֵּית דִּין הַגָּדוֹל בִּלְבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues on רבי יהודה about a tribe's own court
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only rulings of בית דין הגדול create liability for the community offering.

steps.title: Judges know they erred but forgot which ruling it was
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא. The judges know they gave a mistaken ruling but cannot remember which one. Maybe they should still be liable?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: if they knew that they ruled, but they were mistaken about what they ruled, one might think they would be liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that sets up a 'you might have thought' case. This step prepares the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The judges are sure there was a mistaken ruling, so you might think that is enough to bring the offering. The ברייתא raises this possibility only so it can reject it with a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: And they were mistaken, here meaning they forgot
One might think, introducing an idea that will be rejected
The discussion that explains the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
If they knew that they had ruled,
but were mistaken about what they ruled,
phrases.notes: They know a wrong ruling was given, but don't remember which one.

phrases.english: one might think they would be liable?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יָדְעוּ שֶׁהוֹרוּ, וְטָעוּ מָה הוֹרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins with a ברייתא about when the court's error counts as 'known'
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are the judges liable if they know a mistaken ruling was given but not which one?

steps.title: The sin itself must become known
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'and the sin becomes known' teaches that the sin itself must be known. It is not enough for the sinners to know they sinned, so there is no liability here.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And the sin becomes known', and not that the sinners become known.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question with a פסוק: in this case they are not liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'החטאת' (the sin) teaches that the exact sin must be known. In this case people know that a sin was done, but nobody knows which sin it was. So the condition of the פסוק is missing, and no offering is brought.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches, introducing the proof
And the sin becomes known

steps.whatToRemember: The offering is brought only when the exact sin is known. Knowing only that 'someone sinned' is not enough.

phrases.english: The verse says: "And the sin becomes known,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:14

phrases.english: and not that the sinners become known.
phrases.notes: The sinners know they sinned, but which sin it was is not known, so they are not liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'one might think' question of step 7
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They are not liable, because the פסוק requires the sin itself to be known, not just the fact that people sinned.

steps.title: Each sinning tribe brings its own bull
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from 'אשר חטאו' that the number of bulls matches the number of sinning שבטים.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the words 'that they sinned' we learn: if two tribes sinned, they bring two bulls. If three sinned, they bring three.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא starts reading the פסוק closely. It suggests that every שבט that sinned brings its own פר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural wording 'they sinned' suggests the count of offerings goes up with the count of sinners. Here the 'sinners' are understood to be whole שבטים. The next line will test whether this reading is the only possible one.

keyTerms.meaning: 'that they sinned', words from the פסוק about the community's offering
tribes of Israel
bulls brought as offerings

phrases.english: "That they sinned":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:14

phrases.aramaic: חָטְאוּ שְׁנֵי שְׁבָטִים – מְבִיאִין שְׁנֵי פָרִים,
phrases.english: if two tribes sinned, they bring two bulls;
if three sinned, they bring three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section of the ברייתא that explains the views from the משנה about seven tribes in steps 2-4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The number of bulls follows the number of sinning שבטים.

steps.title: Maybe it means individual people, not tribes
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether 'they sinned' might refer to separate individuals, each bringing a פר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps the verse only means: if two individuals sinned, they bring two bulls. If three sinned, they bring three?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises another way to read the same words. Maybe every single sinning person brings a פר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'They sinned' does not say who 'they' are. It could mean tribes, or it could mean individual people. The ברייתא needs another word in the פסוק to settle this, and that is set up for the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'or perhaps it only means', a phrase that raises a different reading
individual people

phrases.english: Or perhaps it only says:

phrases.aramaic: חָטְאוּ שְׁנֵי יְחִידִים – מְבִיאִין שְׁנֵי פָרִים,
phrases.english: if two individuals sinned, they bring two bulls;
if three sinned, they bring three?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the reading in step 9 is the only possible one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does 'they sinned' refer to tribes or to individuals?

steps.title: The word 'congregation' shows it means tribes
steps.stepSummary: The word 'הקהל' teaches that a congregation is liable, and each tribe counts as its own congregation.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'the congregation.' The congregation is liable, and each and every congregation is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question by pointing to the word 'הקהל'. A group, not a single person, brings this offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Single people are not a קהל, so the reading about individuals is ruled out. The phrase 'each and every קהל' tells us that each שבט counts as a separate קהל. That is why each sinning שבט brings its own פר.

keyTerms.meaning: 'the verse teaches', which brings the proof from the פסוק
the congregation
liable, obligated to bring the offering

phrases.english: The verse says: "The congregation":
the congregation is liable,
and each and every congregation is liable.
phrases.notes: Here each שבט counts as its own 'congregation'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'הקהל' shows that groups (שבטים), not individuals, bring the bull, and each שבט counts separately.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: even tribes that did not sin bring a bull
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה explains the details: each sinning שבט brings a פר, and each of the other שבטים also brings a פר because of the sinners.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does this work? If two tribes sinned, they bring two bulls. If seven sinned, they bring seven. And each of the other tribes that did not sin also brings one bull because of them. Even the tribes that did not sin bring an offering because of the sinners. That is why the verse says 'congregation': to make each and every congregation liable. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא spells out how 'each and every קהל' works in practice, following רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a new twist here. Once a majority (seven שבטים) has sinned, even the שבטים that did nothing wrong must bring a פר. In רבי יהודה's view, the whole nation is pulled in by the sin of the majority.

keyTerms.meaning: 'how so?', asking for the practical details
because of them, on account of their sin
the sinners

steps.confusionAlert: The non-sinning שבטים bring a פר only when the sinning שבטים are a majority (like seven). With two sinning שבטים, only those two bring.

phrases.english: How so?

phrases.aramaic: חָטְאוּ שְׁנֵי שְׁבָטִים – מְבִיאִין שְׁנֵי פָרִים,
phrases.english: If two tribes sinned, they bring two bulls;
if seven sinned, they bring seven,
and the rest of the tribes, who did not sin,
bring, because of them, a bull each,
phrases.notes: 'Because of them' means because of the seven שבטים that sinned.

phrases.english: for even those who did not sin
bring because of the sinners.
That is why "congregation" is said:
to make each and every congregation liable.
These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the practical result of the reading in step 11 and names רבי יהודה as its author.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each sinning שבט brings a פר, and when the sinners are a majority, the non-sinning שבטים each bring a פר too.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: the sinning tribes and the court each bring
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says the seven sinning שבטים bring seven bulls and the בית דין adds one more. He learns this by comparing the word 'קהל' in two nearby פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: seven tribes that sinned bring seven bulls, and the court brings one bull because of them. The word 'congregation' is written below and also written above. Just as 'congregation' above means the court together with the congregation, so 'congregation' below means the court together with the congregation.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives רבי שמעון's view, which matches step 4. Only the sinning שבטים bring, plus one פר from the בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון compares the word 'קהל' in פסוק 13 with the same word in פסוק 14. Above, 'the eyes of the קהל' means the judges, and the people are also involved. So below, the offering comes from both the people and the בית דין. Unlike רבי יהודה, the שבטים that did not sin bring nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: below, meaning the later פסוק
above, meaning the earlier פסוק
the court together with the congregation

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: שִׁבְעָה שְׁבָטִים שֶׁחָטְאוּ – מְבִיאִין שִׁבְעָה פָּרִים,
phrases.english: seven tribes that sinned bring seven bulls,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית דִּין מְבִיאִין עַל יְדֵיהֶן פַּר,
phrases.english: and the court brings a bull because of them,
since "congregation" is said below
phrases.notes: 'Below' is the later פסוק, ויקרא 4:14.

phrases.english: and "congregation" is said above.
phrases.notes: 'Above' is the earlier פסוק, ויקרא 4:13.

phrases.english: Just as the "congregation" said above means
the court with the congregation,
so too the "congregation" said below means
the court with the congregation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a view that argues with רבי יהודה in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sinning שבטים each bring a פר, and the בית דין brings one more. The non-sinning שבטים are exempt.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: only the court brings, the people are exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says only the בית דין brings one פר, and the sinning שבטים are exempt. He uses the same comparison of 'קהל' but reads it differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: when seven tribes sinned, the court brings a bull because of them, and the people are exempt. The word 'congregation' is written below and also written above. Just as 'congregation' above means the court and not the public, so 'congregation' below means the court and not the public.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a third view. In רבי מאיר's opinion, the offering is the job of the בית דין alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר uses the same comparison as רבי שמעון but reaches the opposite result. He reads 'the eyes of the קהל' as meaning only the judges. So the קהל that brings the offering is also only the judges, and the people who sinned bring nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: exempt, they do not have to bring
the public, the general people

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון and רבי מאיר use the exact same comparison of the two פסוקים. They argue only about what 'קהל' above means: the court along with the people, or the court alone.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
seven tribes that sinned:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית דִּין מְבִיאִין עַל יְדֵיהֶם פַּר,
phrases.english: the court brings a bull because of them,
and they are exempt,
"congregation" is said below
and "congregation" is said above.
Just as the "congregation" said above means
the court and not the public,
so too the "congregation" said below means
the court and not the public.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same comparison as step 13 but reaches the opposite result.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the בית דין brings one פר, and the sinning people are exempt.

steps.title: What counts as a majority: most people or most tribes
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, quoting רבי מאיר, says a פר is brought if six שבטים that are most of the people sinned, or if seven שבטים sinned even though they are not most of the people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says in רבי מאיר's name: if six tribes sinned and they make up most of the congregation, or if seven tribes sinned even though they do not make up most of the congregation, a bull is brought.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends by defining what 'most of the קהל' means for this offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to reach a majority. One is by population: six large שבטים can hold most of the people. The other is by tribe count: seven out of twelve שבטים is a majority even if they are smaller. Either one is enough to require a פר.

keyTerms.meaning: in his name, quoting someone else
the majority of the congregation
even though

steps.whatToRemember: Three views on seven sinning שבטים: רבי יהודה says the seven bring seven bulls and every other שבט brings one too. רבי שמעון says the seven bring seven, plus one from the בית דין. רבי מאיר says only the בית דין brings one. A majority can be reached either by population or by the number of שבטים.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר מִשְּׁמוֹ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says in his name:
phrases.notes: 'In his name' means he is quoting רבי מאיר, whose view was just given.

phrases.english: if six tribes sinned
and they are the majority of the congregation,
or seven,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ רוּבּוֹ שֶׁל קָהָל –
phrases.english: even though they are not the majority of the congregation,
they bring a bull.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר מִשְּׁמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a definition of 'majority' within רבי מאיר's approach.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A majority can be reached by population (six שבטים) or by number of שבטים (seven), and either one requires a פר.

steps.title: Who holds that the actual sin must be known?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's teaching that the specific sin must become known, and asks which תנא holds this.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'And the sin becomes known.' This means the sin itself must be known, not just that the sinners are known. Who is the תנא who holds this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the ברייתא and asks whose opinion it follows. This sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the בית דין only brings its פר when they know exactly which sin they caused. Knowing only that people sinned is not enough. The גמרא wants to know which תנא would say this, because some תנאים require a קרבן even when the exact sin is unclear.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And the sin becomes known', a phrase from the פסוק about the offering of the community
The sinners
'Who is the תנא?', a question asking whose opinion a teaching follows

phrases.english: The Master said:
"And the sin becomes known"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:14

phrases.english: and not that the sinners become known.
phrases.notes: In other words, knowing that people sinned is not enough. They have to know which sin it was.

phrases.english: Who is the תנא?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר ״וְנוֹדְעָה הַחַטָּאת״ וְלֹא שֶׁיִּוָּדְעוּ הַחוֹטְאִין מַאן תַּנָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to an earlier line of the ברייתא to analyze it, after the opinions about the שבטים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא requires that the specific sin be known before a קרבן is brought.

steps.title: This teaching does not follow רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting רב (or some say רבא), answers that this ברייתא does not follow רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב, and some say it was רבא: this does not follow רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by naming whose opinion the ברייתא does NOT follow: רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer works by elimination. רבי אליעזר does not require knowing the exact sin, so a ברייתא that requires it cannot be his. The proof for this comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Not in line with', meaning this teaching goes against that person's view

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said,
and some say it was Rava:
It is not in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב וְאִיתֵּימָא רָבָא דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מאן תנא question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא is not like רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's view: liable whichever way you look at it
steps.stepSummary: The proof is רבי אליעזר's ruling that a person who ate either חלב or נותר is liable even without knowing which one he ate.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי אליעזר said, whichever way you look at it, he is liable. If he ate חלב, he is liable. If he ate נותר, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source showing that רבי אליעזר does not need the exact sin to be known. The case is a person who had a piece of חלב and a piece of נותר in front of him, ate one, and does not know which one it was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר says it does not matter which piece he ate, because both are forbidden and either one makes him liable for a חטאת. So for רבי אליעזר, knowing you sinned is enough even if you do not know the exact sin. That is the opposite of the ברייתא, which requires the specific sin to be known.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Whichever way you look at it', meaning both possibilities lead to the same result
Forbidden fat of an animal
Meat of a קרבן left over past the time it may be eaten
Liable, here meaning he must bring a חטאת

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר does not mean he is liable for two sins. He ate only one piece. He is liable for one חטאת, because whichever piece it was, it was forbidden.

phrases.english: As we learned:
Rabbi Eliezer said:
Whichever way you look at it:
if he ate forbidden fat, he is liable;
phrases.notes: The case is a person with a piece of חלב and a piece of נותר who ate one but does not know which.

phrases.english: if he ate נותר, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מָה נַפְשָׁךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the claim in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the ברייתא cannot follow רבי אליעזר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אליעזר's ruling on someone who ate either חלב or נותר: he is liable either way, without knowing the exact sin.

steps.title: רב אשי: it can follow רבי אליעזר because of a special פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the ברייתא can follow רבי אליעזר, since here the פסוק says 'אשר חטאו עליה', which stresses knowing the specific sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: you can even say it follows רבי אליעזר. Here is different, because it is written: 'that they sinned regarding it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different answer to the question of whose opinion this is. He says it can be רבי אליעזר after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי agrees that רבי אליעזר normally does not require knowing the exact sin. But for the בית דין's offering the פסוק adds 'אשר חטאו עליה', pointing to a specific sin. So here even רבי אליעזר would require that the exact sin be known.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You can even say', used to show a teaching can fit an opinion that seemed to be ruled out
'Here is different', meaning this case has a special factor
'As it is written', introducing a פסוק

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
You can even say it follows Rabbi Eliezer;
here it is different,
as it is written: "that they sinned regarding it."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:14

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר שָׁאנֵי הָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from step 17, showing the ברייתא can fit רבי אליעזר.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא can follow רבי אליעזר, because the extra phrase 'אשר חטאו עליה' requires knowing the specific sin in the case of the בית דין.

steps.title: The same phrase appears for an individual
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אשי: a similar phrase, 'אשר חטא בה', is written for an individual's חטאת too, yet רבי אליעזר does not require knowing the exact sin there.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, isn't it written: 'that he sinned with it'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב אשי's answer by pointing to a matching phrase in the פסוק about an individual.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'אשר חטאו עליה' requires knowing the exact sin, then 'אשר חטא בה' should require the same for an individual. But רבי אליעזר obligates the individual who ate חלב or נותר without knowing which. So it seems the phrase cannot mean what רב אשי says.

keyTerms.meaning: 'There too', pointing to the other case for comparison
'Isn't it written?', used to raise a challenge from a פסוק

phrases.english: There too, isn't it written:
phrases.notes: "There" means the case of an individual's חטאת, like the one who ate חלב or נותר.

phrases.english: "that he sinned with it"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:23

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's answer in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's reading of 'אשר חטאו עליה' as requiring knowledge of the specific sin.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A similar phrase appears for an individual, yet רבי אליעזר does not require knowing the exact sin there. So the phrase should not require it for the בית דין either.

steps.title: For an individual, the phrase excludes a מתעסק
steps.stepSummary: The phrase for the individual is needed to teach something else: it excludes a מתעסק.
steps.simpleTranslation: That phrase is needed to exclude one who acts without intent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב אשי by explaining that the phrase about the individual is used to teach a different law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For an individual, 'אשר חטא בה' teaches that a מתעסק does not bring a חטאת. Since the phrase there is already used for that, it does not also teach that the exact sin must be known. For the בית דין the phrase is free, so it teaches that the exact sin must be known.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He needs it', meaning the phrase is already used to teach something else
'To exclude', meaning to leave a case out of the law
Someone who does a forbidden act without meaning to do that act at all

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי: the ברייתא can follow רבי אליעזר. For the בית דין, 'אשר חטאו עליה' requires knowing the exact sin. For an individual, the similar phrase is used to exclude a מתעסק, so knowing the exact sin is not required there.

phrases.english: That one is needed
phrases.notes: "That one" is the phrase 'אשר חטא בה' about the individual.

phrases.english: to exclude one who acts without intent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The phrase is needed for a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrases for the individual and for the בית דין are the same, so they should teach the same thing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The individual's phrase is used to exclude a מתעסק, so only the בית דין's phrase teaches that the exact sin must be known.

steps.title: What is רבי יהודה's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the earlier מחלוקת and asks for the source of רבי יהודה's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the opinions about the שבטים and asks how רבי יהודה learns his view. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה said that each sinning שבט brings a פר, and each of the other שבטים also brings a פר because of them (step 12). The גמרא now wants the source in the פסוקים for such a broad view.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is the reason?', asking for the source or logic behind an opinion

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?
phrases.notes: This goes back to רבי יהודה's view from earlier, that each שבט brings its own פר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of רבי אליעזר and returns to רבי יהודה's opinion from step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in the פסוקים for רבי יהודה's view about the שבטים.

steps.title: Four mentions of 'קהל'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds that the word 'קהל' is written four times: 'קהל', 'הקהל', 'קהל', 'הקהל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that four mentions of 'congregation' are written: 'congregation', 'the congregation', 'congregation', 'the congregation'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by showing that רבי יהודה counts four uses of the word 'קהל' in the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word appears twice, but each time it is written as 'הקהל', with the extra letter ה. רבי יהודה counts the plain word and the extra ה as separate teachings, which gives four in total. These extra mentions are the basis for his broader rule that more פרים are brought.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He holds', introducing the view behind someone's opinion
Mentions of the word 'קהל' (congregation)
'Are written'

phrases.english: He holds:
Four mentions of 'congregation' are written:
"congregation," "the congregation,"
phrases.notes: Each 'הקהל' counts twice: once for the word itself and once for the extra ה at the start.

phrases.english: "congregation," "the congregation."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה counts four mentions of 'קהל' (two words, each with an extra ה), which supports his view.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's four lessons from 'קהל'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה uses each of the four mentions of 'קהל' for a different rule: each tribe is liable on its own, the ruling comes from the בית דין while the action comes from the people, tribes that did not sin are drawn along, and a tribe that followed its own tribal court is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: One mention makes each and every congregation liable. One teaches that the ruling depends on the בית דין and the action depends on the congregation. One teaches 'drawing along.' And one teaches about a tribe that acted on the ruling of a בית דין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי יהודה's answer from the last step. It shows what each of the four mentions of 'קהל' teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 counted four mentions of 'קהל'. Now each one gets its own job. Together they support רבי יהודה's view that every tribe brings its own bull, including tribes that did not sin but are pulled along.

keyTerms.meaning: each and every congregation, meaning each tribe on its own
the ruling depends on the בית דין
the action depends on the congregation, the people who did it
'drawing along': tribes that did not sin are pulled in with the tribes that did

steps.confusionAlert: 'גרירה' does not mean the other tribes sinned. They did nothing wrong, yet they are pulled into bringing an offering because the majority sinned.

phrases.aramaic: חַד לְחַיֵּיב עַל כׇּל קָהָל וְקָהָל,
phrases.english: One is to make each and every congregation liable,
phrases.notes: In this sugya each tribe counts as its own 'קהל', so each tribe brings its own bull.

phrases.english: and one is that the ruling depends on the court
and the action depends on the congregation.
And one is for 'drawing along.'
phrases.notes: Tribes that did not sin are drawn after the ones that did, and they bring an offering too.

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד לְשֵׁבֶט שֶׁעָשָׂה בְּהוֹרָאַת בֵּית דִּין.
phrases.english: And one is for a tribe that acted on the ruling of a court.
phrases.notes: This is a tribe that followed the ruling of its own tribal court.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד לְחַיֵּיב עַל כׇּל קָהָל וְקָהָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer from step 23 by giving each of the four mentions of 'קהל' its own lesson.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The four mentions of 'קהל' teach four rules: each tribe is liable, the ruling comes from the court and the action from the people, other tribes are drawn along, and a tribe is liable when it follows its tribal court.

steps.title: רבי שמעון counts only three mentions of 'קהל'
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון holds there are only three mentions of 'קהל' to learn from. He does not learn anything from the extra ה in 'מעיני הקהל', because that wording is just the normal way of speaking.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון holds that three mentions of 'congregation' are written: 'the congregation', 'congregation', 'the congregation'. 'From the eyes of the congregation' is just the way the פסוק speaks, as people say, 'from the eyes of so-and-so.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains where רבי שמעון's view comes from. It starts by showing why he counts three mentions of 'קהל' and not four.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה learned a lesson from both the word 'קהל' and the extra ה each time. רבי שמעון says the ה in 'מעיני הקהל' is not extra. It is simply ordinary speech, like saying 'from the eyes of so-and-so', so no rule is learned from that ה. That leaves him with three: the word 'קהל' above, plus 'קהל' and its ה below.

keyTerms.meaning: three mentions of 'congregation' are written
'from the eyes of the congregation' (ויקרא 4:13)
the normal way the פסוק speaks, so nothing extra is learned from it
so-and-so, some person

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon holds that three mentions of 'congregation' are written:
'the congregation', 'congregation', 'the congregation'.
'From the eyes of the congregation' is just the way the verse speaks,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:13

phrases.english: as people say: 'from the eyes of so-and-so.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי יהודה's source to רבי שמעון's source, and explains why he counts one fewer 'קהל'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון counts three mentions of 'קהל', because 'מעיני הקהל' is ordinary speech and not used for a lesson.

steps.title: How רבי שמעון uses his three mentions
steps.stepSummary: For רבי שמעון, one mention makes each tribe liable. The other two set up a גזירה שוה showing that both the בית דין and the people are involved, so the court brings its own bull together with the tribes.
steps.simpleTranslation: One is to make each and every congregation liable. The other two: 'congregation' is said below and 'congregation' is said above. Just as there it means the court with the congregation, so too here it means the court with the congregation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows what רבי שמעון learns from each of his three mentions of 'קהל'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He agrees with רבי יהודה that one mention makes each tribe liable. He uses the other two for a גזירה שוה that links the 'קהל' bringing the offering to the 'קהל' in the earlier פסוק. That shows the בית דין is counted together with the people, so the court brings a bull too.

keyTerms.meaning: the other two mentions
below / above: the later פסוק and the earlier פסוק
just as there… so too here: the form of a גזירה שוה
the court together with the congregation

phrases.aramaic: חַד לְחַיֵּיב עַל כׇּל קָהָל וְקָהָל,
phrases.english: One is to make each and every congregation liable,
and the other two:
'congregation' is said below,
phrases.notes: 'Below' is the later פסוק, about the congregation bringing the bull (ויקרא 4:14).

phrases.english: and 'congregation' is said above,
phrases.notes: 'Above' is the earlier פסוק, 'מעיני הקהל' (ויקרא 4:13).

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהַלָּן בֵּית דִּין עִם הַקָּהָל –
phrases.english: just as there it means the court with the congregation,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן בֵּית דִּין עִם הַקָּהָל.
phrases.english: so too here it means the court with the congregation.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד לְחַיֵּיב עַל כׇּל קָהָל וְקָהָל, וּתְרֵי אַחֲרִינֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי שמעון's derivation by assigning his three mentions of 'קהל'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One mention makes each tribe liable, and two form a גזירה שוה teaching that the court is included together with the congregation.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why, for רבי שמעון, the tribes bring bulls and the בית דין also brings its own bull.

steps.title: רבי מאיר counts only two mentions of 'קהל'
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר does not learn anything from the difference between 'קהל' and 'הקהל', so he counts only two mentions. He uses them for a גזירה שוה teaching that the offering is the court's alone, not the public's.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר does not learn anything from 'congregation' versus 'the congregation', so two mentions of 'congregation' are written. He needs them to say: 'congregation' is said below and 'congregation' is said above. Just as there it means the court and not the public, so too here it means the court and not the public.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the source for רבי מאיר's view, the last of the three opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון treated 'קהל' and 'הקהל' as separate mentions. רבי מאיר says the extra 'ה' means nothing, so he has only two. His גזירה שוה reads 'קהל' as the בית דין alone, which is why in his view only the court brings the bull and the people are exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: he does not learn a lesson from it
therefore
he needs it for
the court and not the public

steps.whatToRemember: The three views come from how many times each תנא counts 'קהל'. רבי יהודה counts four: each tribe brings a bull and other tribes are drawn along. רבי שמעון counts three: the tribes bring bulls and the court brings one too. רבי מאיר counts two: only the court brings the bull.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון and רבי מאיר use the same גזירה שוה but reach opposite results: 'court WITH the congregation' versus 'court and NOT the public.' Watch the last words of each line.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir does not learn anything from 'congregation' versus 'the congregation',
therefore two mentions of 'congregation' are written.
He needs them for: 'congregation' is said below
and 'congregation' is said above,

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהַלָּן בֵּית דִּין וְלֹא צִבּוּר –
phrases.english: just as there it means the court and not the public,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן בֵּית דִּין וְלֹא צִבּוּר.
phrases.english: so too here it means the court and not the public.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to רבי מאיר's source. He uses the same גזירה שוה as רבי שמעון but reads it as the court alone.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר counts only two mentions of 'קהל' and uses them for a גזירה שוה teaching that the court, not the public, brings the offering.

steps.title: What is the source for רבי שמעון בן אלעזר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reasoning of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר?
steps.whatsHappening: After explaining the views of רבי יהודה, רבי שמעון and רבי מאיר, the גמרא now asks for the source of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view. This line sets up the next step, where the answer comes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds that the court is liable if six tribes sinned and they make up most of the people. It is also liable if seven tribes sinned, even when they are not most of the people. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches this double rule.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? It is a request for the source.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar,
what is his reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי מאיר's derivation to the last opinion, that of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק is the source for רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule about six or seven tribes?

steps.title: Two verses that seem to point in opposite directions
steps.stepSummary: One פסוק, 'מעיני העדה', suggests a minority counts. Another, 'לכל העם', suggests only a majority counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written: 'And it shall be, if from the eyes of the congregation.' This shows that even a minority counts, since it says 'from the eyes.' And it is written: 'For all the people in error.' This shows that a majority counts, but a minority does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by setting two פסוקים side by side that seem to disagree. One suggests a minority is enough, and the other suggests a majority is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מֵעֵינֵי' means 'from' the eyes, so it suggests only part of the people, even a minority. 'לכל העם' means 'all the people.' Since most is treated like all, that phrase means a majority is needed. This sets up a contradiction that the next step will resolve.

keyTerms.meaning: It follows that / apparently.
A minority.
A majority.
That is to say / this comes to teach.

phrases.english: It is written: 'And it shall be, if from the eyes of the congregation' –
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:24

phrases.english: apparently even a minority, since it is written 'from the eyes.'
And it is written: 'For all the people in error,'
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:26

phrases.english: which is to say that a majority, yes,
a minority, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question by bringing the two relevant פסוקים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is two פסוקים: one implies a minority counts, and the other implies only a majority counts.

steps.title: Resolving the verses: six tribes that are most of the people, or seven tribes
steps.stepSummary: Both פסוקים are honored. Six tribes that are most of the people, or seven tribes that are not most of the people, make the court liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If six tribes sinned and they are most of the people, or seven tribes sinned even though they are not most of the people, the court is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how both פסוקים work together, and this completes the source for רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case is a minority in one way and a majority in another. Six tribes are a minority of the tribes but a majority of the people. Seven tribes are a majority of the tribes but may be a minority of the people. Because one פסוק allows a minority, being a majority in just one sense is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? It introduces how two sources fit together.
Most of the people, counted by population.
They are liable to bring an offering.

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, the court is liable if the sinners are a majority in either sense. That means most of the people, even with only six tribes, or most of the tribes, even if they are fewer people.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think one of the cases is a full majority in every way. Each one is only a majority in one sense, and that is enough because 'מעיני' allows some minority.

phrases.english: How so?

phrases.aramaic: עָשׂוּ שִׁשָּׁה וְהֵן רוּבּוֹ שֶׁל קָהָל,
phrases.english: If six sinned and they are the majority of the congregation,
phrases.notes: Six tribes are less than half of the twelve tribes, but they hold most of the people.

phrases.english: or seven, even though
they are not the majority of the congregation, they are liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the apparent contradiction between the two פסוקים from the previous step.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A majority in one sense, either of the tribes or of the population, is enough. 'לכל העם' requires a majority, and 'מעיני' allows some minority element.
